 Published 2 days ago Team Men newcastleunited.com rounds up the latest international call-ups ahead of November's fixture window...
 Malick Thiaw 
 Newcastle United defender Thiaw is part of the Germany squad for their UEFA Nations League fixtures against Serbia and the Netherlands this month.
 The 25-year-old played the full game in Die Mannschaft's 3-1 away win against Serbia at Rajko Mitić Stadium in Belgrade on Friday evening.
 Jürgen Klopp's men return to Berlin's Olympiastadion to face the Netherlands on Monday, 16th November (kick-off 7.45pm GMT), and must secure maximum points in their hopes of securing a quarter-final spot.
 Sean Steur 
 Steur was named in the the Netherlands Under-21s squad for their European Under-21 Championship play-off double-header against Denmark this month.
 Jong Oranje claimed a 3-0 away win in the first leg at the Velje Stadion on Friday, with Steur providing an assist as Holland's youngsters raced into a three-goal lead before the break as the 18-year-old midfielder played 78 minutes, picking up a yellow card on the stroke of half-time. 
 T he second leg takes place at the Yanmar Hanasaka Stadion in Almere on Tuesday, 17th November (kick-ofr 5:30pm GMT).
 Aladji Bamba 
 Midfielder Bamba is part of the France Under-21s squad for their friendlies against Italy and England.
 Les Bleuets suffered a 2-1 home defeat against Italy at the Stade Francis Le Basser in Laval on Friday evening, with Bamba featuring from the bench in the 79th minute.
 France will face a clash with England at Bristol City's Ashton Gate on Monday, 16th November (kick-off 7.30pm GMT).
 Alex Murphy and Rory Finneran 
 The Magpies pair have both been named in the Republic of Ireland Under-21s squad ahead of this month's European Under-21 Championship two-legged play-off against Finland.
 The Boys in Green, who finished in second place of Group D, were beaten 1-0 at Tampere's Tammelan Stadion in their first leg on Friday afternoon. 
 Murphy and Finneran both played the full game, with the latter picking up a yellow card in the final minutes.
 Ireland's youngsters host Finland at Turner's Cross in Cork on Tuesday, 17th November (kick-off 5:45pm GMT) as Murphy and Finneran, who completed respective season-long loan moves to FC Kaiserslautern and Notts County last summer, will be aiming to help their country qualify for the competition's finals for the first time in their history.
 Yoane Wissa 
 Magpies frontman Wissa was on target for DR Congo in their 3-1 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Sierra Leone on Thursday.
 The 30-year-old struck early on to give his side a fourth minute lead at the Stade des Martyrs in Kinshasa, volleying home with precision inside the box to give his side an advantage they didn't look in danger of relinquishing.
 Having netted his 14th goal for his country, he was taken off with seven minutes remaining and will now hope to feature against the same opposition at El Jadida's Ben M'Hamed El Abdi Stadium on Tuesday, 17th November (kick-off 4pm GMT).
 Dan Burn and Lewis Hall 
 Burn, a late addition to Thomas Tuchel's England squad, joined Lewis Hall in the starting line-up for their UEFA Nations League win over Croatia on Thursday.
 Both players completed the full 90 minutes of the 2-1 victory at Wembley, turning in fine, resolute displays at the back as Harry Kane's clincher on his record 126th Three Lions appearance saw them beat Slaven Bilić's men.
 They then head to the Riyadh Air Metropolitano in Madrid to face Spain on Sunday, 15th November for a game that may well prove decisive in who takes top spot in Group C.
 Hall had already been named in the squad last week and will be looking to win his ninth caps for his country, having featured against Czechia and Croatia in September and October, while Burn - part of the England squad that reached the World Cup semi-finals last summer - now has 12 caps to his name.
 Amar Dedić 
 Dedić has been named in the Bosnia and Herzegovina squad for this month's UEFA Nations League fixtures against Sweden and Romania.
 The 24-year-old defender, who has accrued 31 senior caps for his country, could be in action when the Dragons face Sweden at Stockholm's Strawberry Arena on Saturday, 14th November before hosting Romania at Zenica's Bilino Polje three days later.
 Both matches will take place at 7:45pm GMT.
 Lukas Horníček 
 The Magpies goalkeeper was named in the Czechia squad for their UEFA Nations League fixtures against Spain and Croatia, and stayed on the bench for their 2-0 defeat to the former on Thursday.
 Horníček, who made his competitive senior debut for his country in September's reverse fixture against Croatia, will be aiming to add to his three caps as Repre face Croatia at the Opus Arena in Osijek on Sunday, 15th November (kick-off 7:45pm GMT). 
 Bazoumana Touré 
 The former Hoffenheim winger was on the bench for the Ivory Coast as they won 2-1 in the first of two Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Gambia.
 Touré was unused at the Stade de la Paix in Bouaké on Thursday, and will now look to feature in the two sides' second meeting at the Independence Stadium in Bakau on Tuesday, 17th November (kick-off 4pm GMT). 
 Ousmane Diabaté 
 On-loan Gençlerbirliği midfielder Diabaté won his fourth senior cap for Guinea in their 2-1 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier at home to Eritrea on Thursday.
 The 19-year-old, who has been in fine form during his temporary stint in the Turkish top flight, played the full game in Conakry, and could now feature against the same side at the Al Salam Stadium in Cairo on Tuesday, 16th November (kick-off 5pm GMT).
 Sean Neave 
 The Winlaton-born teenager, currently on a season-long loan with Wolverhampton Wanderers, received his first call-up for England Under-20s ahead of their two EURO Elite League fixtures.
 The Young Lions, currently occupying top spot in the nine-team table, thrashed Czechia 6-1 in Mansfield on Thursday, with the 19-year-old coming off the bench for the final 18 minutes.
 Neave's side now head to Portugal for their second game on Monday, 16th November (kick-off 4pm GMT) at the Estadio Municipal de Mafra.
 Roman Dowell and Kyran Thompson 
 The Magpies Academy pair were named in the England Under-18s squad ahead of three fixtures in Spain this month.
 In the Young Lions 3-2 win over the Netherlands on Wednesday, 11th November, Dowell was an unused substitute while Thompson came on for the final quarter of an hour.
 They will now take on Sweden on Saturday, 14th November (kick-off 11am GMT) before England's youngsters conclude their camp against Switzerland on Monday, 16th November (kick-off 3pm GMT), with all games taking place at the Oliva Nova venue in Valencia.
 Anthony Elanga 
 Elanga will be part of the Sweden squad for their UEFA Nations League clashes with Bosnia and Herzegovina and Poland in November.
 The Strawberry Arena in Stockholm is the venue for the Blågult 's game against Bosnia on Saturday, 14th November, before their trip to the Tarczyński Arena in Wrocław for the Poland game on Tuesday 17th November.
 Both games kick off at 7.45pm GMT.
 Will Osula 
 Denmark's UEFA Nations League campaign reaches its conclusion this month, with Osula in line to feature against Portugal and Norway.
 Braga's Estádio Municipal is the venue for the Portugal clash on Saturday, 14th November (kick-off 7.45pm GMT), with Osula's side returning to Copenhagen to face Norway at Parken on Tuesday, 17th November. That Group D match will also kick-off at 7.45pm GMT.
 Matheos Ferreira 
 Ashington-born youngster Ferreira has received his first call-up to the Brazil Under-20s squad ahead of their friendly double-header against Peru.
 The teenager has been in fine form for United's under-23 side, and has been rewarded with his first call up to the Seleção youth set-up - for which he is eligible through his Brazilian father.
 Ferreira - who is also eligible for Italy courtesy of his Italian mother - made his first team bow during the Magpies' pre-season draw at Gateshead in July.
